, a clinical intelligence company transforming clinical trials with AI-powered precision analytics in the pharmaceutical industry, today announced the appointment of Kevin Felix as Strategic Advisor, strengthening the senior strategic and institutional experience surrounding the Company as NetraMark advances its commercialization strategy.

Mr. Felix brings more than 25 years of senior leadership experience across capital markets, asset management, corporate strategy and securities law. Most recently, Mr. Felix served as President of the Investment Office of Global Atlantic Financial Group, responsible for all business management and operational matters related to the firm’s $175 billion investment portfolio. Prior thereto, his senior positions at Scotiabank included President and CEO of Scotia Capital (USA) Inc. and Global Head of Fixed Income, Currencies, and Commodities, a diverse multi-billion dollar business throughout North and South America, Europe and Asia. Mr. Felix also brings extensive corporate governance experience, having served as independent director for several firms.

“Kevin has operated at a high level within the global financial markets,” said George Achilleos, CEO of NetraMark. “As we advance commercialization and broaden the Company’s relationships across the pharmaceutical and investment communities we are continuing to strengthen the level of experience around the organization. Kevin is an exceptional addition.”

“NetraMark has developed a highly differentiated approach to applying artificial intelligence to one of the pharmaceutical industry’s most significant challenges: understanding patient heterogeneity within clinical trials,” said Kevin Felix, Strategic Advisor to NetraMark. “I am excited to work with George and the NetraMark team as they continue building the Company, developing important industry relationships and evaluating the strategic and capital markets opportunities that may accompany its growth.”
Supporting NetraMark’s Next Stage of Growth

As Strategic Advisor, Mr. Felix will advise NetraMark on various matters including Canadian and U.S. institutional investor and investment banking relationships, strategic transactions, corporate development and longer-term capital markets strategy.
Mr. Felix holds a Masters of Law in Securities Regulation from Georgetown University Law Center, a Juris Doctor, cum laude, from New York Law School, and a Bachelor of Arts from Bucknell University.

About NetraAI

NetraAI is engineered to include focus mechanisms that separate small datasets into explainable and unexplainable subsets. Unexplainable subsets are collections of patients that can lead to suboptimal overfit models and inaccurate insights due to poor correlations with the variables involved. NetraAI uses explainable subsets to derive insights and hypotheses (including factors that influence treatment and placebo responses and adverse events), potentially increasing the likelihood of a clinical trial's success. Many other AI methods lack these focus mechanisms and assign every patient to a class, often leading to "overfitting," which drowns out critical information that could have been used to improve a trial's chance of success.
About NetraMark

NetraMark is focused on being a leader in the development of Generative Artificial Intelligence (Gen AI)/Machine Learning (ML) solutions that are targeted at the biotechnology and pharmaceutical industries. The Company's product offering uses a novel topology-based algorithm that has the ability to parse patient data sets into subsets of people that are strongly related according to several variables simultaneously. This allows NetraMark to use a variety of ML methods, depending on the character and size of the data, to transform the data into powerfully intelligent data that activates traditional AI/ML methods. The result is that NetraMark can work with much smaller datasets often prevalent in clinical trials, and accurately segment diseases into different types, as well as help to classify patients for sensitivity to drugs and/or efficacy of treatment.
